assignments.belief: A wolf came right into my kitchen and stole one of my chickens. I saw the beast with my own eyes.
assignments.reasoning: She was the sole witness in her own kitchen and has no reason to doubt what she saw.

assignments.belief: Maren lost a chicken from her kitchen. She says it was a wolf, but it was more likely a fox or a stray dog — a wolf would not get into the village centre on my watch.
assignments.reasoning: Maren reported it to him as garrison captain, but he reframes the wolf as a lesser animal to protect the garrison's reputation.

assignments.belief: Maren says a great grey wolf walked straight into the kitchen and ran off with a whole chicken in its jaws, bold as a lord.
assignments.reasoning: He works the inn stables and Maren told him at once; kitchen talk fattened the wolf and the drama.

assignments.belief: I have heard nothing unusual from the village today.
assignments.reasoning: The chapel is on the hill with no proximity; Osric will not advertise a wolf on his watch, and Maren has not climbed the hill over one chicken.

assignments.belief: The woods are as they always are. I have had no word from anyone.
assignments.reasoning: Bell is a hermit in the deep woods with no ties and no proximity, so nothing from the village can reach him.

summary: Maren saw the theft and immediately told Tam, then reported it to Osric, who downplayed the wolf; the story never reached Ilva on the hill or Bell in the woods.
